Hi Ben —

Thanks for the proposal. Before we sign up for a reserved pool we need to validate how the capacity maps to our workload. Can you share a concrete acceptance plan (what tests you run, pass/fail criteria) and a commissioning timeline for provisioning GPUs and routing traffic?

High-level items we care about:
- Expected sustained RPS and 99th/95th latency targets under the committed pool
- Soak test length and rollback criteria
- Who runs the traffic generation and how keys/traffic segregation are handled
- Expected lead time for provisioning dedicated GPUs after contract signature

I've attached our initial capacity matrix (greenbank-capacity-reqs-v2.xlsx) with expected peak concurrency and token mixes. Procurement looped in for any commercial questions.

Julia
Julia Park
Director, AI Platform
GreenBank Financial

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — capacity validation questions

Hi Julia —

Appreciate the matrix, that helps a lot. Draft plan below — high level acceptance steps and an initial commissioning timeline. We can tighten durations once we confirm exact GPU type and region.

Acceptance plan (summary):
1) Staging provisioning (dedicated pool mirrored to production config) — we provision a staging pool identical to the reserved GPU pool.
2) Synthetic workload validation (run by Redwood SRE + GreenBank SRE) — run 72-hour soak with 3 traffic patterns: baseline, peak burst, and worst-case long-seq prompts. Pass criteria: 99th latency under target, no OOM or error-rate > 0.5%.
3) Prefix/KV cache warm-up — use replay of 24 hrs production traces; verify cache hit-rate targets and token-cost estimates.
4) Ramp to production traffic with 2-day canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) using weighted routing and automatic fallback to hosted API for errors.

Commissioning timeline (provisional):
- Contract signed: T+0
- GPU pool provisioning (infra): T+5 business days (hardware allocation + image bake)
- Staging cluster up: T+7 business days
- Synthetic soak: T+9 to T+12 business days
- Canary ramp: T+13 to T+15 business days
- Full cutover: T+16 business days

Questions for you (short):
- Which GPU SKU do you plan to commit to? (A100-80GB / H100 / L4 etc.)
- Are your production latency SLOs at 95th, 99th, or both?
- Any regulatory controls for transfer of telemetry to Redwood?

Laura — can you review commercial lead times for the pool commit and confirm if we can meet T+5? Grace / Jonas — can you validate the soak and canary windows for ops runbook?

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Sep 22, 2026 at 10:03 AM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> Draft plan below — high level acceptance steps and an initial commissioning timeline.

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifications:
- GPU SKU: H100 preferred for latency-sensitive models, but we can consider mixed pools if cost mandates.
- SLOs: 95th = 120ms, 99th = 300ms for our main chat surface.
- Telemetry: we cannot forward raw PII traces to external telemetry systems; it has to be redacted or sampled. Our security team will share exact compliance constraints.

Procurement: our target signature date is 2026-10-01 (internal approval permitting). If we hit that date, can Redwood align the provisioning to a T+5 lead time? That would put cutover mid-October which is tight but doable if ops window is available.

Julia

Julia —

Thanks — good to have the SLOs and rough sign date. Per your target signature on 2026-10-01, updated concrete timeline below (calendar dates):

Updated commissioning calendar (assuming signature 2026-10-01 end-of-day):
- 2026-10-06: Infra allocation & GPU assignment (we block H100 nodes in us-west-2)
- 2026-10-08: Staging cluster ready; image bake + network configs
- 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-13: Synthetic soak (72 hours + verification window)
- 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-16: Canary ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback gates
- 2026-10-19: Final cutover review and go/no-go. Full production traffic ideally 2026-10-20

Operational notes:
- We'll run the 72-hour soak using your sample traces but with PII redaction steps agreed in advance. Grace, Jonas — we'll need a short runbook (5-7 steps) for traffic generation and failure injection.
- Cost model: committing to N H100 nodes will lower unit token costs; Laura I'll attach a one-page commit proposal (proposed-gpu-commitment.pdf) for procurement to review.
- Fallback: during the canary we keep hosted API fallbacks for all requests to avoid user-facing errors.

If the signature slips beyond 10/01 we'll push the cutover by business days accordingly. Let me know if GreenBank needs an overlap period where both hosted and dedicated run concurrently for billing reconciliation.

Ben
